title: Preventing S-Trap Siphoning with Proper Trap Arm Length
description: The water seal in a P-trap acts as a critical barrier against sewer gases entering living spaces. A common hazard occurs when the trap arm drops vertically before reaching a vented branch, turning a P-trap into an unvented S-trap. This setup creates self-siphoning, pulling the protective water seal out of the trap dip as waste flows. To maintain a functional seal, ensure the trap arm remains horizontal for a minimum distance equal to twice the pipe diameter before connecting to a vertical vent line, following local plumbing code rules.

Preventing S-Trap Siphoning with Proper Trap Arm Length

The water seal in a P-trap acts as a critical barrier against sewer gases entering living spaces. A common hazard occurs when the trap arm drops vertically before reaching a vented branch, turning a P-trap into an unvented S-trap. This setup creates self-siphoning, pulling the protective water seal out of the trap dip as waste flows. To maintain a functional seal, ensure the trap arm remains horizontal for a minimum distance equal to twice the pipe diameter before connecting to a vertical vent line, following local plumbing code rules.
